figure_checks.source_of_marks: render_panel.py:75-94 calls nova.media.poloidal.draw_nulls twice, which draws the magnetic axis filled (poloidal.py:604-617 passes color=style.axis_color with no facecolor override), the admitted X-point as a filled cross (poloidal.py:618-663) and the strike points as discs; render_panel.py:95-105 then overlays a hollow triangle on the reference axis. The hollow overlay's transparent interior lets the filled grey below show through, which is why the legend's hollow swatch matches nothing in the panel.

findings.disposition: folded: a follow-up plan section on converged-forward-solve adding the X-point and strike-point entries to the panel legend for all three panels
findings.evidence: image-0.png rendered pixels; render_panel.py:75-94 draws the nulls through draw_nulls while the legend at 107-136 lists flux and axis only
findings.summary: The legend keys four marks -- analytic flux, solved flux, analytic axis, solved axis -- while the panels draw two further mark types, the admitted X-point and the strike points, which appear in the render unkeyed. On image-0 the X-point is the grey cross at the bottom of the vessel (eroded blob x 647..652, y 632..637), and it is the mark that makes the row a diverted single-null case rather than a limited one; the legend gives the reader no entry for it, and the evidence text does not name it either. A reader can see the field, so nothing is hidden, but cannot tell from the figure what the cross is. The panel is otherwise the clearest of the three and the defect does not hold the node.

findings.disposition: folded: the same follow-up plan section, which should either draw the reference axis hollow only or draw both axes as keyed
findings.evidence: image-1.png and image-0.png rendered pixels; render_panel.py:95-105,111-129; nova/media/poloidal.py:604-617
findings.summary: The 'analytic axis' legend swatch is drawn hollow, but in every panel the analytical axis renders as a solid grey triangle. draw_nulls draws the axis filled (poloidal.py:604-617) and the hollow overlay at render_panel.py:95-105 has a transparent interior, so the filled grey shows through and the hollow cue is lost. Measured on image-1, the analytic axis is a solid grey triangle occupying x 728..740, y 381..393, about 18 px tall, against a solid blue solved triangle about 10 px tall at x 744..751. The two axes are therefore separated by colour and by size, not by the hollow-against-filled distinction the key promises -- and colour alone fails for a colour-blind reader. The marks remain distinguishable in these renders, so the defect is recorded rather than blocking.

findings.disposition: exempted: the coincidence is the measurement, and thickening the reference to make it visible would misrepresent which field is the answer
findings.evidence: image-2.png rendered pixels: no grey contour pixels outside the axis mark region; evidence fragment private section states the coincidence
findings.summary: The legend names a dashed grey 'analytic flux', and no dashed grey contour is visible anywhere in the panel: the eight drawn contours are all solid blue. That is the correct depiction of a state whose two fields coincide to 4.7e-15, and the caption says so in words ('The solved and reference contours are indistinguishable at this level array'), but a reader who has the figure alone may read it as a reference that was never drawn. Drawing the reference beneath the solved line at a thinner weight, or adding one dashed segment called out as coincident, would make the absence a statement rather than an ambiguity.

findings.summary: The panel occupies a small minority of the canvas. Measured non-white ink between y 150 and y 690 spans 27.3 % of the 1399 px width on image-0, 23.5 % on image-1 and 21.9 % on image-2, because the poloidal axes are held at equal aspect inside a 14 x 7.2 in landscape canvas (render_panel.py:49,106). The legend row spans x 305..1093, roughly twice the panel's width. The consequences are drawn detail: on image-0 the solved contours crowd into overlapping strokes at the outboard wall and the knot at the bottom null is hard to follow at the delivered size. The 14 x 7.2 canvas is the repository's slide size, so this is a call about fitting a portrait panel to it rather than a styling error.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: None of the three captions only repeats its figure's title. Each carries its own row's terminal residual, converged flag, axis coordinates and the direction of the discrepancy, and the panels carry no titles of their own, so identity comes from the file name and the caption.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Four findings, none blocking. No label is clipped, none overlaps another label or the data, and no text is unreadable, so none of the blocking categories is met. The defects are that three mark types drawn in the panels (the X-point, the strike points and, in effect, the analytic axis as a filled rather than hollow triangle) are not keyed as the legend shows them, and that the converged panel's reference contours are invisible because they coincide with the solved ones.
item_verdicts.rendered_artifact: All three attachments were opened and inspected as images at their native 1399x720 size; verdicts were formed from the rendered pixels, and no SVG was opened, listed, searched, rendered or shown. The reviewed head removed the PNG twins (748ae9fcb deletes the three .png files), so the attachments are the reviewer-supplied renders of the three committed panels rather than files still tracked at the head.
